note: No Bible verse is quoted in the bio, so references is empty. Price's own sayings carry scriptural echoes, kept as HIS words but worded in the familiar SUV register: 'leading my people into the ditch' (Matt 15:14) → 'nikiwaongoza watu wangu shimoni'; 'Jesus Christ and Him crucified' (1 Cor 2:2) → 'Yesu Kristo, naye amesulibiwa' (the SUV phrase, also found in the shipped corpus); 'still, small voice' (1 Kings 19:12) → 'sauti ndogo tulivu' (the corpus's usual phrase); 'not what you believe, but in whom you believe' echoes 2 Tim 1:12 (rendered freely).

Clock time: 'About four o'clock that afternoon' → 'Yapata saa nne alasiri ile': the printed hour (four) is kept per house rule, NOT converted to Swahili reckoning (which would be saa kumi). A Swahili reader will read 'saa nne alasiri' oddly (saa nne is normally 10 a.m.); the reviewer may prefer 'saa kumi jioni'. 'At midnight' → 'saa sita usiku' (no printed number).

'Four Minute Men', 'Lodi Gospel Team', 'Bethel Temple', 'Denman Arena', church names (First Congregational Church, First Baptist Church, Metropolitan Methodist Church), 'Wesley College', 'Free Methodist' and the Monroe Street Bridge ('Daraja la Monroe Street') keep their English names; the book titles The Story of My Life, The Real Faith and the magazine Golden Grain stay in English.
The sermon title 'Divine Healing Bubble Explodes' is translated ('Kiputo cha Uponyaji wa Kiungu Chapasuka') because it is a sermon title in a newspaper advertisement, not a published work.

'whispered that she was calling for sinners': Swahili pronouns have no gender, so 'she' (McPherson, the preacher) is rendered 'mhubiri' to keep the reference clear; otherwise 'yeye' would read as the prominent minister.
'explaining God away' → 'akitoa maelezo yaliyomweka Mungu kando' (the sense: explaining things so that God was set aside).

Terms follow the Wigglesworth/Bosworth bios: uponyaji wa kiungu, ubatizo/kubatizwa katika Roho Mtakatifu, Kipentekoste, Kikongregesheni; altar call → 'mwito wa madhabahuni'; crippled → 'viwete/kiwete'; arenas → 'kumbi kubwa' / 'ukumbi mkubwa wa michezo'; tabernacle → 'ukumbi wa mikutano'; 'the prairies' → 'mikoa ya Prairies'; 'an institution' kept vague as 'taasisi', as in the English.
